outcomes.secondary: disagreement_label at an absolute shift >= 1.0 pChEMBL
outcomes.rationale: Continuous magnitude preserves information discarded by a threshold and permits robust regression; binary risk remains a secondary operational view.

validation.study_grouped: 5-fold GroupKFold by connected study-compound components, so neither publications nor molecules cross folds
validation.leave_target_out: one complete ChEMBL target per fold
leakage_constraints: held-out publication groups never enter training
temporal training years strictly precede test years
only prior_* assay/protocol evidence is eligible
natural-product status is evaluated as a subgroup and is not a predictor

methods.constant: training-fold prevalence plus training-fold median disagreement magnitude
methods.historical_beta: Jeffreys-smoothed prior cross-publication contradiction rate and prior document-median range
methods.legacy_logistic: the existing binary classifier feature contract, refit inside each development fold
methods.huber_magnitude: robust Huber regression on log1p magnitude with prior historical evidence
methods.rf_history: random-forest magnitude regression using prior historical evidence
methods.rf_protocol: the same random forest plus molecular descriptors and prior-only protocol completeness features

huber.prediction_bounds: zero to maximum magnitude observed in that training fold

uncertainty.random_forest_interval: 10th to 90th percentiles across trees; descriptive ensemble interval, not a calibrated coverage guarantee

implementation_amendment.reason: One forward-time Huber fit hit its fixed optimizer limit and extrapolated far beyond the training outcome range.
implementation_amendment.change: Increase only the optimizer iteration ceiling and apply training-range bounds to Huber predictions. This numerical-stability correction is fixed for every fold and does not alter features, outcomes, RF hyperparameters, validation splits, candidate selection, or readiness criteria.

required: study-grouped PR-AUC point estimate > observed prevalence
study-grouped MAE lower than the constant-median baseline
directionally consistent performance in forward-temporal validation
no evidence that protocol features degrade natural-product results relative to rf_history
readiness_rule.interpretation: Failure of any criterion means the method is not ready for a new independent test. Confidence intervals and subgroup sample size must be reported rather than used to relax the rule.
